source_contexts.statement: AgNS extinction fitted by Gaussian (R²=0.972) and Lorentzian (R²=0.997) curves; these are source fit qualities, not particle-size measurements.
Reactant Ag nanoparticle solution spectra right after synthesis and after one month at ambient room temperature; distinct from SI p.1 optional 4 °C pre-etch storage.

source_contexts.locator: SI PDF p.4, Figure S5a–c; main PDF p.5
source_contexts.statement: Before/after Ag surface XPS supports oxidized surface states; pre-etch PXRD is dominated by fcc Ag. Do not claim bulk Ag2O, oxide thickness, or identity of individual imaged particles.
Precipitate Cu 2p3/2 XPS is assigned to CuO, distinct from Cu, Cu2O, and CuCl2; precipitate is not the AgNS surface.

Cu(II)-mediated etching rounds Ag particles within 15 min in a kinetic comparison (three repeats); standard synthesis reaction still runs 2 h. Conventional comparison exceeds 3 h; panel b shows a 250 nm ascorbic-acid-associated peak.

conflictPairs.text: Main p.2 reports 67% AgNC and 33% right bipyramid after flocculation; SI Figure S1c labels 66.98% and 32.02%, which sum to 99.00%. Preserve source statements without normalization.
SI Figure S10 caption describes green (c) and red (d) PL distributions, but the artwork labels these panels b and c; sample links follow visible panels and note the caption error.

bindings.caption: NanoXtalSyn-authored apparatus schematic. A 20 mL glass vial is stirred during CTAC preheat and sequential AgNO3/NaBH4 additions; the 2–3 nm seed range is reported, not a drawn scale.

bindings.caption: NanoXtalSyn-authored apparatus schematic. The capped 20 mL glass vial shows the sequential seed/AgTFA addition and later ascorbic-acid growth phase; the cap is source-reported.

bindings.caption: NanoXtalSyn-authored apparatus schematic. BDAC-treated capped vial rests undisturbed in a 30 °C oven after removal of the stir bar; rod/wire flocculate is separated from supernatant.

bindings.source_locator: SI PDF p.1, Synthesis of silver nanospheres, post-flocculation wash
bindings.caption: NanoXtalSyn-authored apparatus schematic. The selected supernatant, rather than the rod/wire flocculate, is transferred to a 50 mL centrifuge tube for two spins and redispersion.

bindings.caption: NanoXtalSyn-authored apparatus schematic. SDS/PVP addition precedes the 0.2 µm syringe membrane filter; the filtered sample moves to a 50 mL tube for centrifugation and redispersion.

bindings.caption: NanoXtalSyn-authored apparatus schematic. The Cu(I) negative control uses an acetonitrile/water mixture because Cu(I) is not soluble in water; precursor, ratio and dose are unreported.

general_background.title: Formation from dissolved precursors
general_background.summary: When dissolved species become supersaturated with respect to a solid, nucleation and growth can compete with continued precursor conversion. Mixing, complexation and solution chemistry can change that balance.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Mechanisms of Nucleation and Growth of Nanoparticles in Solution

general_background.title: From a metal precursor to reactive species
general_background.summary: A metal precursor supplies the metal, while its ligands and conversion chemistry influence how reactive species become available. Stronger or more persistent coordination can slow release of reactive metal species, while ligand exchange can open alternative conversion pathways.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Mechanisms of Nucleation and Growth of Nanoparticles in Solution

general_background.title: Electron transfer from a reductant
general_background.summary: A reducing agent can supply electrons that change the oxidation state of a precursor. Coordination and competing reactions affect how that electron transfer contributes to particle formation.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Recent Advances in the Liquid-Phase Syntheses of Inorganic Nanoparticles
